newsitem.title: USA: Clinton expected to visit Arkansas on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Clinton expected to visit Arkansas on Tuesday.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was expected on Tuesday to visit his home state of Arkansas, which has been struck by deadly tornadoes, a White House official said on Sunday.

The official, who asked not to be identifed, said a news conference that Clinton had scheduled for 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT) on Tuesday would likely be postponed until later in the week, probably until Friday.

The White House official also said Clinton was expected to declare a disaster area in parts of Arkansas later on Sunday, saying the White House was waiting for a formally documented request from the state itself before he could do so.

Deadly tornadoes struck southwestern Arkansas on Saturday, killing 23 people and injuring hundreds of others, according to Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee. Federal officials were not immediately able to confirmed the figures.

Earlier on Sunday, Clinton aide Bruce Lindsey told reporters the president was planning to go to Little Rock "if it is appropriate" and was likely to declare the state a disaster area so it can qualify for emergency federal aid.

Several hospitals in south and central Arkansas reported treating scores of storm-related injuries, many of them serious. In some areas, electrical power and telephone service was lost when uprooted trees snapped utility lines.
